name: dvd-vr
desc: Utility to identify and extract recordings from DVD-VR files
why: Pokes at the DVD-VR recording file format to pull out recordings, a small but genuine dive into an obscure format.

brief.what_it_is: dvd-vr is a command-line utility that reads the DVD-VR navigation data on a disc and lists the recordings it contains. Per the page, it can identify recordings and optionally copy them out. Its input is a path to a VR_MANGR.IFO file on a mounted disc, such as /media/dvd/DVD_RTAV/VR_MANGR.IFO. Its output is a text report giving the format version, per-VOB video and audio parameters (TV system, resolution, MPEG2, AC-3 audio), and for each program a title, date, VOB format number, and size in bytes.
brief.why_it_exists: The DVD-VR format is used by DVD recorders and camcorders, and the author wrote the tool in February 2007 by reverse engineering DVD-VR discs. The page describes the goal as identifying and optionally copying recordings from such a disc.
brief.how_it_works: The tool parses the VR_MANGR.IFO navigation file on the disc and reports the format version (the example shows DVD-VR V1.1), the VOB stream parameters, and the program list. The page does not explain the parsing internals beyond this.

commands_seen.context: Example run from the homepage. Points the tool at the VR_MANGR.IFO navigation file on a mounted DVD-VR disc and prints the format, VOB details, and list of recordings.

brief.install_notes: The homepage offers a download of V0.9.7 (28K) and a Source link, but the page text gives no build or install steps. Nothing in the page mentions extra runtimes or accounts. The tool needs a mounted DVD-VR disc or a copy of its files. The page says it has been tested on Linux, Mac OS X, and Windows via WSL or Cygwin.
brief.standout: It targets a niche consumer disc format that most rippers ignore, and it was built by reverse engineering rather than from a published spec. The example output shows Japanese title text, so it handles non-ASCII titles.
brief.status: Quiet. The latest listed release is V0.9.7, and the page footer carries a copyright line dated Aug 24 2010. The page links a ChangeLog, but I did not open it, so I cannot confirm the most recent change date.
brief.caveats: The page only describes the tool as a 'DVD-VR ripper for linux' in its title and says it has been tested on Mac OS X and Windows through WSL or Cygwin, so native Windows and Mac support are unclear. Licensing is not stated on the page; it only says 'open source'. The README-equivalent text is short and documents one example run, with no list of options or flags beyond the file argument.
quotes: dvd-vr is a utility to identify and optionally copy recordings from a DVD-VR format disc
This open source program was created in Feb 2007 by reverse engineering DVD-VR format discs
